protocol_evidence.paraphrase: Random baseline is a simple random sample of 150 records and is the primary agreement/sufficiency population.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Target size: 150 records. Purpose: estimate register-wide human-LLM agreement, disagreement, and register sufficiency. Selection: simple random sampling without replacement from all eligible register records after removing only the frozen training/pilot exclusion set. The baseline is drawn before any hard-case sample so that it is not depleted of model-disagreement records. Use: primary agreement and sufficiency estimates. At n=150, a proportion near 50% has an approximate 95% margin of error of about +/-8 percentage points. This is a descriptive precision statement, not a power calculation for replacement-alpha differences.

protocol_evidence.paraphrase: Register sufficiency specifies individual coder-rating distributions, record-majority ratings, and broad/strict subsets.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Register sufficiency: individual coder-rating distributions and record-level majority ratings, reported separately for the random baseline and hard-case samples; sizes of the broad and strict sufficiency subsets.

protocol_evidence.paraphrase: Taxonomy fit specifies individual and record-majority distributions and conditions taxonomy-issue frequencies on Partial Fit or No Fit responses.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Taxonomy fit: individual and record-level majority ratings of Fit, Partial Fit, No Fit and Cannot assess from register entry. Cannot assess will be reported separately as an evidence-sufficiency outcome and will not be counted as No Fit, as a taxonomy defect, or in taxonomy-issue denominators. Taxonomy-issue frequencies will be reported among responses coded Partial Fit or No Fit.

protocol_evidence.paraphrase: Record-majority diagnostic ratings require at least two coders to choose the same category; splits remain separate.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Record-level majority diagnostic ratings will be assigned only where at least two of the three scratch coders select the same response category. Where all three coders select different categories, the record will be reported as No majority / split judgement rather than being resolved by ordering, averaging or assigning an intermediate category. This rule applies to register sufficiency and taxonomy fit. It does not alter the separately defined broad and strict register-sufficiency subset rules in Section 8.3.

protocol_evidence.paraphrase: Unclear reporting includes coder-specific use, majority use, and coherence with sufficiency/confidence.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Unclear from Register Entry: coder-specific use, majority use, and coherence patterns with sufficiency and confidence.

protocol_evidence.paraphrase: The protocol explicitly prescribes 95% Wilson score intervals for baseline proportions and record bootstrap percentile intervals for agreement families.
protocol_evidence.recorded_text: Baseline proportions will use 95% Wilson score intervals. Agreement metrics, replacement differences, delta_min, and eligible per-label metrics will use 2,000 nonparametric record-level bootstrap resamples with percentile intervals and SEED_BOOTSTRAP = 20260714. Percentiles and percentile bootstrap interval endpoints use Hyndman–Fan Type 7 interpolation, equivalent to NumPy/Pandas linear quantile interpolation where those implementations are used. All ratings for a record remain together, and alpha_ABC, all replacement alphas, differences, and delta_min are recalculated jointly within each resample.
